Read with care: this run uses ~1/36 of the native receivers and a coarser mesh than the paper (15 GB RAM ceiling -- see baseline_report.md). The tan surface is the real per-station topography. Numbered markers (#1-#6) sit at each body's actual RECOVERED peak in the IMPROVED model specifically (same position shown under both layers, so it doesn't jump when you switch -- baseline's own recovered peaks sit somewhere slightly different; see src/validation.py's centroid_offset_m for that difference numerically), not a digitised guess at ground truth. See baseline_report.md's "Data and Ground Truth" section for the approximate true positions used only to know which recovered feature is which body. Improved run caveat (see improved_report.md's "Sign check"): every body's correctly-signed peak in the improved model sits next to a larger-magnitude opposite-sign artifact -- a real finding, not a display bug, if the improved layer looks messier than the baseline.
